correctness.rationale: For cyclic angular gaps x,y,z,w summing 2pi, the Ptolemy identity sin((x+y)/2)sin((y+z)/2)=sin(x/2)sin(z/2)+sin(y/2)sin(w/2) gives Q=sin(x/2)sin(z/2)/[sin(x/2)sin(z/2)+sin(y/2)sin(w/2)]. The monotone relation z -> Q at fixed x,y has derivative B sin(y/2)/[2sin^2((y+z)/2)]>0, and its inverse gives a Jacobian ~4 epsilon log(1/epsilon)sin^2(y/2) at x=epsilon^u, q=epsilon v for interior 0<u,v<1. Combined with the EXACT Dirichlet gap density 3/(4pi^3), the unnormalized marked density is (3/pi^3)epsilon log(1/epsilon)sin^2(y/2). The established Martin cross-ratio marginal has P(Q<epsilon)~(3/pi^2)epsilon log(1/epsilon); after normalization the interior limit density is sin^2(y/2)/pi. The u>1 boundary pointwise density is negligible; Scheffé yields total variation, not just weak convergence. Root angle Phi is independent and uniform by rotational symmetry. Independently checked Ptolemy numerical equality for positive gaps; evaluated normalization int_0^{2pi}sin^2(y/2)/pi dy=1. The source proof establishes the final claim despite being covered by other published work.

Under the Dirichlet(1,1,1,1) angular gaps, swap the third and fourth gaps: the exact quadrilateral Ptolemy ratio Q(x,y,z,w) becomes the chord intersection fraction U(x,y,w,z) of the published theorem. The swap preserves the JOINT law of X and Y, as well as the Dirichlet sampling law, so its marked total-variation theorem gives exactly the claimed U_epsilon=log X/log epsilon, V=Q/epsilon and sine-square Y law.
